title: Production debugging and technical trade-offs
exp: These questions test whether you own production problems or defer them. The strongest answers describe something REAL from your work.
pts: Check data first, then code, then infrastructure. The most common root cause of a 10x slowdown is a data change.
Bug corrupting 2% of records for 3 months: order matters -- stop damage, scope blast radius, communicate, plan backfill.
SQL Server vs Spark: RDBMS for transactional/small/ACID workloads. Spark when data doesn't fit on one machine.
Technical debt: deliberate and documented debt is fine. Silent debt is what compounds into a crisis.

viz.note: Debugging order: data first (volume? skew? type change?) -> code (recent deploy?) -> infrastructure (Spot? OOM?). Never assume infrastructure first.

qa.q: A Spark job that ran fine for 6 months suddenly takes 10x longer. Walk through your investigation.
qa.a: Check data first: did input volume change? Did a new skewed key appear? Did a source send malformed records causing type coercion? Only after ruling out data: did a recent deploy change the query? In Spark UI: which stage got slow, is one task an outlier (skew), did a new Exchange appear in the plan?

qa.q: You discover a bug corrupting 2% of records for 3 months. What order do you act in?
qa.a: (1) Deploy the fix to stop further corruption. (2) Scope the blast radius -- which records, sources, time period, downstream consumers. (3) Communicate proactively before being asked. (4) Plan and execute backfill. Don't do all at once -- stop the bleeding, understand scope, communicate, fix history, in that order.
